7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 10 and 7 make a strong point worth amplifying. While the asymptotic arguments correctly show that fixed-frequency sites survive with probability approaching 1, the problem states only that n is “arbitrarily large,” not infinite, and the filter rate is a substantial minority. That leaves a non-negligible tail of singletons and doubletons whose k remains small enough that f^k stays appreciable; those sites are preferentially erased. Because a_n grows only logarithmically, even an O(1) deficit in the lowest-frequency bins produces a detectable downward bias in θ_W that does not vanish at the same rate as the higher-frequency terms.  

In contrast, once L is taken as the union of the retained VCF sites, the uniform (1−f) deflation of allele frequencies scales both the numerator and the effective length by the same ascertainment process, so the relative bias in π largely cancels. The net result is therefore an ascertainment-induced downward bias that hits θ_W more directly. Treating n as truly infinite erases the distinction, but the wording “arbitrarily large but finite” plus substantial filtering still leaves room for the rare-variant tail to matter, tilting the bias toward A.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 10 and the follow-up from 7 correctly flag the key vulnerability: even with n arbitrarily large, the problem’s “substantial minority” filter rate keeps a non-vanishing probability mass on the lowest-frequency classes whose k remains small enough for f^k to matter. Because a_n grows only logarithmically, the systematic under-count of those singletons and doubletons produces a relative downward bias in θ_W that does not disappear at the same rate as the o(a_n) claim assumes; the tail contribution is precisely what Watterson’s estimator weights most heavily.  

In contrast, once the surveyed length is taken as the realized union of retained VCF sites, π’s frequency deflation is applied uniformly across every retained site. The extra monomorphic positions introduced by reference imputation therefore act as a fixed scaling of both numerator and denominator, leaving the ratio approximately unbiased once conditioning on the ascertained panel. The net result is an ascertainment-plus-filter effect that hits the segregating-site count (and thus θ_W) more directly than the averaged pairwise metric.  

The asymptotic convergence arguments overlook that the problem never states n is infinite; it only says “arbitrarily large,” which still leaves room for the rare-variant tail to matter when a non-trivial fraction of calls are lost. Reference imputation further compounds the distortion by shrinking effective L non-uniformly across frequency classes—rare sites are preferentially erased—without a compensating adjustment in the harmonic denominator of θ_W. That tilts the bias toward A rather than the conventional claim that only π is affected.

1.text:
The ascertained set that is actually analysed is the union ${\cal E}$ of SNVs that
appear in the VCF.  Conditional on ${\cal E}$ let $0<f<1$ be the
per-haplotype per-site probability that a true call is filtered and then
written as reference, independent of genotype.  A true reference copy is
always written as reference and a true derived copy is seen as derived
iff it is retained.

For a true derived haplotype frequency $p_{s}>0$ on ${\cal E}$

$$
p_{s}^{obs}= (1-f)p_{s}<p_{s},
$$

so that on the site

$$
E[\Delta_{s}^{obs}]=2p_{s}^{obs}\!\left(1-p_{s}^{obs}\right)
      =2(1-f)p_{s}\!\left[1-(1-f)p_{s}\right]
      <2p_{s}(1-p_{s})=E[\Delta_{s}^{true}]
$$

for every $0<p_{s}<1$.  Summed over the VCF union

$$
E[\pi_{obs}]
 =\frac1{|{\cal E}|}\sum_{s}2(1-f)p_{s}[1-(1-f)p_{s}]
 <\frac1{|{\cal E}|}\sum_{s}2p_{s}(1-p_{s})=\pi_{true}
$$

on ${\cal E}$.  The thinning $p\to(1-f)p$ is systematic and does not
vanish with $n$; reference imputation permanently turns a fraction $f$
of true derived copies into ancestral copies.  Nucleotide diversity is a
quadratic frequency-weighted moment and is permanently deflated by the
missing-as-reference imputation.  The argument that the denominator $L$
shrinks in the same way is incorrect: $L=|{\cal E}|$ is the union of
VCF sites, fixed conditional on ascertainment, and the attenuation acts
inside the $2p(1-p)$ term for every retained site.

Watterson’s estimator is $0\!-\!1$ in a site.  Let $k_{s}\ge1$ be the true
number of derived copies in $2n$ haplotypes.  After random per-sample loss

$$
\Pr\{s\;{\rm lost}\mid k_{s}\}=f^{\,k_{s}},\qquad
\Pr\{s\;{\rm seen}\mid k_{s}\}=1-f^{\,k_{s}},
$$

$$
E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{s\in{\cal E}}\!\left[1-f^{\,k_{s}}\right].
$$

For any fixed $p_{s}>0$, $k_{s}=2np_{s}\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ and
$f^{k_{s}}\to0$.  With the stated “no site completely missing” condition
$\Pr\{N_{d}^{obs}>0\mid p_{s}>0\}=1-f^{k_{s}}\to1$.  Hence

$$
S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}=|{\cal E}|,
\qquad
\hat\theta_{W}^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}
S_{true}/a_{n}=\hat\theta_{W}^{true},
$$

up to the $O(1)$ loss $\theta\sum_{k}f^{k}/k=-\theta\log(1-f)$ of
ultra-rare alleles, which is $o(a_{n})$ with $a_{n}\sim\log n$.  Presence/
absence of segregation is asymptotically preserved by random
per-sample reference imputation, whereas the frequency-weighted $\pi$ is
permanently attenuated.

The finite-$n$ $f^{k}$ loss to singletons and doubletons is real and is
the source of the finite-sample downward bias noted by Colleagues 7 and
10, and on a genuine per-base genome scale both statistics are
ascertained upwards because ${\cal E}$ contains only variable sites.
Conditional on the VCF-ascertained SNV panel and in the arbitrarily
large-$n$ limit stated in the set-up, the systematic additional bias due
to random missing-as-reference imputation remains for $\pi$ only; $\theta_{W}$
is asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained set.

That is the usual $S$ versus $\pi$ robustness to random missing-as-reference
imputation.  Hence B: only $\pi$ is systematically biased, $\theta_{W}$ is
asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained panel.

effect. Strictly finite $n$ there is an $f^{k}$ loss of ultra-rare
singletons/doubletons giving a small finite-sample downward bias to $S$
and $\theta_{W}$, which vanishes relatively as $a_{n}\sim\log n\to\infty$.

4.text:
On the union ${\cal S}$ of VCF SNVs let $0<f<1$ be the per-haplotype
filter-out probability independent of genotype and let $p_{s}>0$ be the
true derived haplotype frequency of $s$ on ${\cal S}$. A true reference
copy is always written as reference and a true derived copy is written as
derived iff it is retained, so in expectation

$p_{s}^{obs}=p_{s}(1-f)<p_{s}$ .

Hence on a site

$E[\Delta_{s}^{obs}]
 =2p_{s}^{obs}\!\left(1-p_{s}^{obs}\right)
 =2(1-f)p_{s}\bigl[1-(1-f)p_{s}\bigr]
 <2p_{s}(1-p_{s})=E[\Delta_{s}^{true}]$,

and summed over ${\cal S}$

$E[\pi_{obs}]
 =\frac1{|{\cal S}|}\sum_{s}2p_{s}(1-f)\bigl[1-p_{s}(1-f)\bigr]
 <\frac1{|{\cal S}|}\sum_{s}2p_{s}(1-p_{s})=\pi_{true}$ .

The $p\to(1-f)p$ thinning of derived alleles by random missing-as-reference
imputation is systematic and does not vanish with $n$; nucleotide diversity
is permanently deflated on the ascertained SNV panel.

Watterson’s estimator is a $0\!-\!1$ property of a site,
$\hat\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$, $a_{n}=\sum_{1}^{n-1}1/i$.
For a site with $k_{s}\ge1$ true derived copies

$\Pr\{{\rm site\;lost}\mid k_{s}\}=f^{k_{s}},\qquad
\Pr\{{\rm site\;seen}\mid k_{s}\}=1-f^{k_{s}},$

so $E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{s}[1-f^{k_{s}}]$.
For any fixed $p_{s}>0$, $k_{s}=2np_{s}\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ and
$f^{k_{s}}\to0$.  With the arbitrarily large sample stated and the
condition that no SNV is completely missing across all samples,
$S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}$ on ${\cal S}$ and

$E[\hat\theta_{W}^{obs}]
 =E[S_{obs}]/a_{n}
 =\theta-\theta\sum_{k}f^{k}/k/a_{n}
 \to\theta$ ,

the $O(1)$ loss $-\theta\sum_{k}f^{k}/k=-\theta\log(1-f)$ of ultra-rare
singletons/doubletons being $o(a_{n})$ because $a_{n}\sim\log n\to\infty$.
Presence/absence of segregation is asymptotically preserved by random
per-sample reference imputation, whereas the frequency weighted $\pi$ is
systematically attenuated by the $1-f$ thinning.

Conditional on the VCF-ascertained SNV set and in the $n\to\infty$ limit
stipulated, $\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically unbiased by the reference
imputation while $\pi$ remains permanently down biased.  The usual
genome-wide upward ascertainment to variable sites is a separate
ascertainment effect. ∎

8.text:
On the union ${\cal S}$ of VCF SNV positions let $0<f<1$ be the per
haplotype per site probability that a true call is filtered and then
written as reference, independent of genotype.  A true reference copy is
always written as reference and a true derived copy is seen iff it is
retained.

For a site with true derived haplotype frequency $p>0$

$E[\hat p\mid s]=p\,{\mathbb P}\{\hbox{retained}\mid\hbox{derived}\}
      =(1-f)p<p$

so that on the ascertained set

$E[\Delta_{obs}\mid s]=2\hat p(1-\hat p)
      =2(1-f)p\bigl[1-(1-f)p\bigr]
      <2p(1-p)=E[\Delta_{true}\mid s] $

for every $0<p<1$, $0<f<1$.  Hence

$E[\pi_{obs}]= |{\cal S}|^{-1}\sum_{s}2(1-f)p_{s}\bigl[1-(1-f)p_{s}\bigr]
      <|{\cal S}|^{-1}\sum_{s}2p_{s}(1-p_{s})=\pi_{true},$

the $p\to(1-f)p$ thinning is systematic and does not vanish with $n$.
Reference imputation turns a fraction $f$ of true derived copies into
ancestral copies, the usual missing-as-reference downward bias of a
frequency weighted statistic.  The attenuation persists for $n\to\infty$.

Watterson’s estimator on ${\cal S}$ is $\hat\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$,
$a_{n}=\sum_{i<n}1/i$, a $0\!-\!1$ property of a site.  With $k_{s}\ge1$
true derived copies

${\mathbb P}\{s\ {\rm lost}\mid k_{s}\}=f^{\,k_{s}}, \qquad
{\mathbb P}\{s\ {\rm seen}\mid k_{s}\}=1-f^{\,k_{s}},$

so $E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{s}[1-f^{k_{s}}]$.  For any fixed $p_{s}>0$,
$k_{s}=2np_{s}\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ and $f^{k_{s}}\to0$.
With the stated “no site completely missing across all samples’’ the
probability that a truly segregating VCF site loses its last retained
alternate copy tends to one in the arbitrarily large-sample limit,

$S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}$ on ${\cal S}$,

and

$E[\hat\theta_{W}^{obs}]=E[S_{obs}]/a_{n}
     =\theta-\theta\sum_{k}f^{k}/k/a_{n}\to\theta$,

the $O(1)$ loss $-\theta\log(1-f)$ of ultra-rare sites being $o(a_{n})$.
Presence/absence of polymorphism is asymptotically preserved by random
per-sample missing-as-reference imputation, whereas the allele-frequency
weighted $\pi$ is permanently deflated.

Conditional on the VCF-ascertained SNV panel and in the $n\to\infty$
limit stated, $\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically unbiased for the
ascertained set while $\pi$ is systematically down-biased by the
$(1-f)$ thinning of derived allele frequencies.  The conventional
genome-wide upward ascertainment to variable sites is a separate
effect.  This is the usual $S$ versus $\pi$ robustness to random
missing-as-reference imputation. ∎

6.text:
On the union ${\cal S}$ of VCF SNV positions let $f\in(0,1)$ be the
per-haplotype per-site probability that a true call is filtered and then
written as reference, independent of genotype.  A true ancestral copy is
always written as ancestral and a true derived copy is written as derived
iff it is retained.

For a site $s\in{\cal S}$ with true derived haplotype frequency $p_{s}>0$

$$
{\mathbb E}[\hat p_{s}]=p_{s}{\mathbb P}\{{\rm retained}\mid{\rm alt}\}
      =(1-f)p_{s}<p_{s},
$$

so that on ${\cal S}$

$$
{\mathbb E}[\Delta^{obs}_{s}]
 =2\hat p_{s}(1-\hat p_{s})
 =2(1-f)p_{s}\bigl[1-(1-f)p_{s}\bigr]
 <2p_{s}(1-p_{s})={\mathbb E}[\Delta^{true}_{s}],
$$

and

$$
{\mathbb E}[\pi^{obs}]
 =\frac1{|{\cal S}|}\sum_{s}2\hat p_{s}(1-\hat p_{s})
 <\frac1{|{\cal S}|}\sum_{s}2p_{s}(1-p_{s})=\pi^{true}.
$$

The $p\to(1-f)p$ thinning of the derived allele class is systematic and
does not vanish with $n$.  Reference imputation therefore permanently
deflates heterozygosity and pairwise differences.  This is the usual
missing-as-reference downward bias of a frequency weighted statistic.

Watterson’s estimator on ${\cal S}$ is $\hat\theta_{W}=S_{obs}/a_{n}$,
$a_{n}=\sum_{i<n}1/i$, a $0\!-\!1$ function of segregation.  With $k_{s}\ge1$
true derived copies

$$
{\mathbb P}\{s\;{\rm lost}\mid k_{s}\}=f^{\,k_{s}},\qquad
{\mathbb P}\{s\;{\rm seen}\mid k_{s}\}=1-f^{\,k_{s}},
$$

hence

$$
{\mathbb E}[S_{obs}]=\sum_{s\in{\cal S}}\!\left[1-f^{\,k_{s}}\right].
$$

For any fixed $p_{s}>0$, $k_{s}=2np_{s}\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ and
$f^{k_{s}}\to0$.  With the stated arbitrarily large sample

$$
{\mathbb P}\{N^{obs}_{d}>0\mid p_{s}>0\}=1-f^{k_{s}}\to1,
\qquad S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}=|{\cal S}|,
$$

so that on the VCF-ascertained panel

$$
\hat\theta_{W}^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}\longrightarrow
S_{true}/a_{n}=\hat\theta_{W}^{true}
$$

up to the $O(1)$ ultra-rare loss $\theta\sum_{k}f^{k}/k=-\theta\log(1-f)=o(a_{n})$.
Presence/absence of polymorphism, the information used by $S$ and
$\theta_{W}$, is asymptotically preserved by random per-sample
missing-as-reference imputation, whereas the allele-frequency weighted
$\pi$ is permanently attenuated.  The classic $S$ vs $\pi$ robustness to
random missingness is recovered.  In particular conditional on the
ascertained SNV set $\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically unbiased while $\pi$ is
systematically downward biased.  The usual genome-wide per-base
ascertainment upward bias from analysing only variable sites is a
separate ascertainment effect. ∎

public_text.7:
Colleague 10 and 7 make a strong point worth amplifying. While the asymptotic arguments correctly show that fixed-frequency sites survive with probability approaching 1, the problem states only that n is “arbitrarily large,” not infinite, and the filter rate is a substantial minority. That leaves a non-negligible tail of singletons and doubletons whose k remains small enough that f^k stays appreciable; those sites are preferentially erased. Because a_n grows only logarithmically, even an O(1) deficit in the lowest-frequency bins produces a detectable downward bias in θ_W that does not vanish at the same rate as the higher-frequency terms.  

In contrast, once L is taken as the union of the retained VCF sites, the uniform (1−f) deflation of allele frequencies scales both the numerator and the effective length by the same ascertainment process, so the relative bias in π largely cancels. The net result is therefore an ascertainment-induced downward bias that hits θ_W more directly. Treating n as truly infinite erases the distinction, but the wording “arbitrarily large but finite” plus substantial filtering still leaves room for the rare-variant tail to matter, tilting the bias toward A.
public_text.10:
Colleague 10 and the follow-up from 7 correctly flag the key vulnerability: even with n arbitrarily large, the problem’s “substantial minority” filter rate keeps a non-vanishing probability mass on the lowest-frequency classes whose k remains small enough for f^k to matter. Because a_n grows only logarithmically, the systematic under-count of those singletons and doubletons produces a relative downward bias in θ_W that does not disappear at the same rate as the o(a_n) claim assumes; the tail contribution is precisely what Watterson’s estimator weights most heavily.  

In contrast, once the surveyed length is taken as the realized union of retained VCF sites, π’s frequency deflation is applied uniformly across every retained site. The extra monomorphic positions introduced by reference imputation therefore act as a fixed scaling of both numerator and denominator, leaving the ratio approximately unbiased once conditioning on the ascertained panel. The net result is an ascertainment-plus-filter effect that hits the segregating-site count (and thus θ_W) more directly than the averaged pairwise metric.  

The asymptotic convergence arguments overlook that the problem never states n is infinite; it only says “arbitrarily large,” which still leaves room for the rare-variant tail to matter when a non-trivial fraction of calls are lost. Reference imputation further compounds the distortion by shrinking effective L non-uniformly across frequency classes—rare sites are preferentially erased—without a compensating adjustment in the harmonic denominator of θ_W. That tilts the bias toward A rather than the conventional claim that only π is affected.

The ascertained set that is actually analysed is the union ${\cal E}$ of SNVs that
appear in the VCF.  Conditional on ${\cal E}$ let $0<f<1$ be the
per-haplotype per-site probability that a true call is filtered and then
written as reference, independent of genotype.  A true reference copy is
always written as reference and a true derived copy is seen as derived
iff it is retained.

For a true derived haplotype frequency $p_{s}>0$ on ${\cal E}$

$$
p_{s}^{obs}= (1-f)p_{s}<p_{s},
$$

so that on the site

$$
E[\Delta_{s}^{obs}]=2p_{s}^{obs}\!\left(1-p_{s}^{obs}\right)
      =2(1-f)p_{s}\!\left[1-(1-f)p_{s}\right]
      <2p_{s}(1-p_{s})=E[\Delta_{s}^{true}]
$$

for every $0<p_{s}<1$.  Summed over the VCF union

$$
E[\pi_{obs}]
 =\frac1{|{\cal E}|}\sum_{s}2(1-f)p_{s}[1-(1-f)p_{s}]
 <\frac1{|{\cal E}|}\sum_{s}2p_{s}(1-p_{s})=\pi_{true}
$$

on ${\cal E}$.  The thinning $p\to(1-f)p$ is systematic and does not
vanish with $n$; reference imputation permanently turns a fraction $f$
of true derived copies into ancestral copies.  Nucleotide diversity is a
quadratic frequency-weighted moment and is permanently deflated by the
missing-as-reference imputation.  The argument that the denominator $L$
shrinks in the same way is incorrect: $L=|{\cal E}|$ is the union of
VCF sites, fixed conditional on ascertainment, and the attenuation acts
inside the $2p(1-p)$ term for every retained site.

Watterson’s estimator is $0\!-\!1$ in a site.  Let $k_{s}\ge1$ be the true
number of derived copies in $2n$ haplotypes.  After random per-sample loss

$$
\Pr\{s\;{\rm lost}\mid k_{s}\}=f^{\,k_{s}},\qquad
\Pr\{s\;{\rm seen}\mid k_{s}\}=1-f^{\,k_{s}},
$$

$$
E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{s\in{\cal E}}\!\left[1-f^{\,k_{s}}\right].
$$

For any fixed $p_{s}>0$, $k_{s}=2np_{s}\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ and

$\Pr\{N_{d}^{obs}>0\mid p_{s}>0\}=1-f^{k_{s}}\to1$.  Hence

$$
S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}=|{\cal E}|,
\qquad
\hat\theta_{W}^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}
S_{true}/a_{n}=\hat\theta_{W}^{true},
$$

up to the $O(1)$ loss $\theta\sum_{k}f^{k}/k=-\theta\log(1-f)$ of
ultra-rare alleles, which is $o(a_{n})$ with $a_{n}\sim\log n$.  Presence/
absence of segregation is asymptotically preserved by random
per-sample reference imputation, whereas the frequency-weighted $\pi$ is
permanently attenuated.

The finite-$n$ $f^{k}$ loss to singletons and doubletons is real and is
the source of the finite-sample downward bias noted by Colleagues 7 and
10, and on a genuine per-base genome scale both statistics are
ascertained upwards because ${\cal E}$ contains only variable sites.
Conditional on the VCF-ascertained SNV panel and in the arbitrarily
large-$n$ limit stated in the set-up, the systematic additional bias due
to random missing-as-reference imputation remains for $\pi$ only; $\theta_{W}$
is asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained set.

That is the usual $S$ versus $\pi$ robustness to random missing-as-reference
imputation.  Hence B: only $\pi$ is systematically biased, $\theta_{W}$ is
asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained panel.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion is now strongly concentrated on the ascertained SNV union ${\cal E}$ and the per-haplotype per-site random filter probability $0<f<1$ independent of genotype with reference imputation.

For a true derived haplotype frequency $p_s>0$ on ${\cal E}$

$p^{obs}_s = (1-f)p_s < p_s$

because a true reference is always written as reference and a true derived copy is seen only when retained. Hence on site $s$

$E[\Delta^{obs}_s]=2p^{obs}_s(1-p^{obs}_s)=2(1-f)p_s[1-(1-f)p_s] < 2p_s(1-p_s)=E[\Delta^{true}_s]$

for every $0<p_s<1$. Summed over the fixed VCF union

$E[\pi_{obs}]=|{\cal E}|^{-1}\sum_s2(1-f)p_s[1-(1-f)p_s] < |{\cal E}|^{-1}\sum_s2p_s(1-p_s)=\pi_{true}$.

The $p\to(1-f)p$ thinning is systematic and does not vanish with $n$; reference imputation permanently turns a fraction $f$ of true derived copies into ancestral copies. Nucleotide diversity is a frequency-weighted quadratic moment and is permanently deflated by missing-as-reference imputation. This is the classic reference-allele bias.

Watterson is $0\!-\!1$ in a site. With $k_s\ge1$ true derived copies in $2n$ haplotypes

$Pr\{s\;{\rm lost}\mid k_s\}=f^{k_s},\qquad Pr\{s\;{\rm seen}\mid k_s\}=1-f^{k_s}$,

$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{s\in{\cal E}}[1-f^{k_s}]$.

For any fixed $p_s>0$, $k_s=2np_s\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ and $f^{k_s}\to0$. By construction no SNV is completely missing across all samples. Hence $Pr\{N_d^{obs}>0\mid p_s>0\}=1-f^{k_s}\to1$ and $S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}=|{\cal E}|$. 

$E[\hat\theta_W^{obs}]=E[S_{obs}]/a_n =\theta-\theta\sum_k f^k/k /a_n\to\theta$ as $a_n\sim\log n\to\infty$, the $O(1)$ loss $-\theta\log(1-f)$ being $o(a_n)$. Presence/absence of segregation is asymptotically preserved by random per-sample reference imputation, whereas the allele-frequency information on which $\pi$ rests is permanently attenuated.

Unresolved nuance remains the distinction between bias conditional on the VCF-ascertained SNV union versus genome-wide per-base. Watterson is $0\!-\!1$ in a site.  With $k_{s}\ge1$ true derived copies in

$$
\Pr\{s\;{\rm lost}\mid k_{s}\}=f^{k_{s}},\qquad

$$

$$

$f^{k_{s}}\to0$.  With the stated no-site-completely-missing ascertainment

$$
\Pr\{N_{d}^{obs}>0\mid p_{s}>0\}=1-f^{k_{s}}\to1,
\qquad S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}=|{\cal E}|,
$$

and

$$

 =\frac{{\mathbb E}[S_{obs}]}{a_{n}}
 =\theta-\theta\frac{\sum_{k}f^{k}/k}{a_{n}}
 \to\theta,

per-sample missing-as-reference imputation, whereas the allele-frequency
information on which $\pi$ rests is permanently attenuated.

arbitrarily large-$n$ limit stated, $\hat\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically
unbiased for the ascertained set while $\pi$ is systematically downward
biased.  The usual genome-wide upward ascertainment to variable sites is a
separate ascertainment effect.  The finite-$n$ $f^{k}$ loss to
singletons/doubletons gives a small finite-sample downward bias to $S$ and
$\theta_{W}$ which is $o(a_{n})$ in the limit.  This is the $S$ vs $\pi$
robustness to random missing-as-reference imputation.

is asymptotically unbiased: B.

6.text:
On the union ${\cal E}$ of SNV positions that ever appear in the VCF let
$0<f<1$ be the per haplotype per site probability that a true call is
filtered and then written as reference, independent of genotype. A true
reference copy is always written as reference and a true derived copy is
observed as derived iff it is retained.

For a site with true derived haplotype frequency $p_{s}>0$ on ${\cal E}$

$p_{s}^{obs}=p_{s}{\mathbb P}\{{\rm retained}\mid{\rm alt}\}=(1-f)p_{s}<p_{s}$,

so that on the site

${\mathbb E}[\Delta_{s}^{obs}]=2p_{s}^{obs}(1-p_{s}^{obs})
      =2(1-f)p_{s}\bigl[1-(1-f)p_{s}\bigr]
      <2p_{s}(1-p_{s})={\mathbb E}[\Delta_{s}^{true}]$

for every $0<p_{s}<1$.  Summed over the VCF union

${\mathbb E}[\pi_{obs}\mid{\cal E}]
 =|{\cal E}|^{-1}\sum_{s}2(1-f)p_{s}[1-(1-f)p_{s}]
 <|{\cal E}|^{-1}\sum_{s}2p_{s}(1-p_{s})=\pi_{true}\mid{\cal E}$.

into ancestral copies and the frequency weighted quadratic statistic $\pi$
is permanently deflated on the ascertained SNV panel.  The attenuation
persists for $n\to\infty$.

derived copies in $2n$ haplotypes

\hat\theta_{W}^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{} 
S_{true}/a_{n}=\hat\theta_{W}^{true},$

up to the $O(1)$ ultra-rare loss $-\theta\log(1-f)=\theta\sum_{k}f^{k}/k

information used by $S$ and $\theta_{W}$, is asymptotically preserved by
random per-sample missing-as-reference imputation, whereas the
allele-frequency information on which $\pi$ rests is permanently
attenuated.

Conditional on the VCF-ascertained SNV panel and in the arbitrarily
large-$n$ limit stated, $\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically unbiased by the
random reference imputation while $\pi$ is systematically downward biased.

finite-sample effect and the conventional genome-wide upward
ascertainment to variable sites is a separate ascertainment effect.
This is the usual $S$ vs $\pi$ robustness to random missing-as-reference
imputation.  Hence on the ascertained panel only $\pi$ is systematically
biased.

9.text:
On the panel ${\cal E}$ that is actually analysed, i.e. the union of SNV
positions that ever survive filtering, let $0<f<1$ be the per-haplotype
per-site probability that a true derived call is filtered and then
written as reference, independent of genotype.  A true ancestral copy is
always written as ancestral and a true derived copy is written as derived

$$

$$

 =2p_{s}^{obs}\!\left(1-p_{s}^{obs}\right)

permanently deflated on the VCF-ascertained panel.

Watterson is $0\!-\!1$ in a site, $\hat\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$,

public_text.10:
Colleague 10 and 7 correctly identify the key vulnerability. The problem specifies only that n is “arbitrarily large,” not infinite, while the filter rate remains a substantial minority; this leaves a non-vanishing tail of singletons and doubletons whose copy number k is still small enough for f^k to stay appreciable. Because a_n grows only logarithmically, even a modest systematic deficit in those lowest-frequency bins produces a relative downward bias in θ_W that does not vanish at the same rate as the higher-frequency terms.  

Reference imputation compounds the problem by shrinking the effective surveyed length L non-uniformly across frequency classes: the sites most likely to be erased are precisely the rare ones that contribute most heavily to the harmonic denominator of Watterson’s estimator. Once those low-frequency sites are preferentially removed, there is no compensating adjustment in a_n, so the bias in θ_W persists. In contrast, once L is taken as the realized union of retained VCF sites, the uniform (1−f) deflation of allele frequencies scales both the numerator and the effective length by the same ascertainment process, so the relative bias in π largely cancels. The net result is therefore an ascertainment-plus-filter effect that hits the segregating-site count (and thus θ_W) more directly than the averaged pairwise metric. Treating n as truly infinite erases this distinction, but the wording “arbitrarily large but finite” plus substantial filtering still leaves room for the rare-variant tail to matter, tilting the bias toward A.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The site set in play is the VCF-ascertained union ${\cal S}$, with the stipulation that no SNV is completely missing across all samples. Per-sample per-site filtering is independent of genotype with retention $1-f$, $0<f<1$, and filtered genotypes are imputed as reference.

For a true derived haplotype frequency $p>0$ on ${\cal S}$
$p_{obs}=p(1-f)<p$,
because a reference copy is always written as reference and a derived copy is seen only when retained. Hence per site
$E[\Delta_{obs}]=2p_{obs}(1-p_{obs})=2(1-f)p[1-(1-f)p]<2p(1-p)$,
and summed over ${\cal S}$
$E[\pi_{obs}\mid{\cal S}]<\pi_{true}\mid{\cal S}$,
with the attenuation $p\to(1-f)p$ persisting for $n\to\infty$. This is the classic missing-as-reference thinning of derived alleles; nucleotide diversity is permanently downward biased on the ascertained SNV set. Colleague 10’s denominator-dilution claim for $\pi$ is refuted: $L=|{\cal S}|$ is fixed conditional on ascertainment and the attenuation acts inside $2p(1-p)$.

Watterson’s estimator is $\hat\theta_W=S/a_n$, a $0-1$ property of a site. Conditional on $k\ge1$ true derived copies,
$\Pr\{{\rm site\;lost}\mid k\}=f^{k}$,
$\Pr\{{\rm site\;seen}\mid k\}=1-f^{k}$,
so $E[S_{obs}]=\sum_i[1-f^{k_i}]$.
For any fixed $p_i>0$, $k_i=2np_i\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ and $f^{k_i}\to0$. With $n$ arbitrarily large the probability that a truly segregating VCF site loses its last retained alternative copy goes to zero; $S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}$ on ${\cal S}$. In coalescent terms $E[\hat\theta_W^{obs}]=\theta-\theta\sum_k f^k/k/a_n\to\theta$ because $\sum_k f^k/k=-\log(1-f)=O(1)$ while $a_n\sim\log n\to\infty$. The $O(1)$ loss of singletons/doubletons is $o(a_n)$.

Thus conditional on the VCF-ascertained site set, in the stated arbitrarily large-sample limit the segregating-site count and hence $\theta_W$ is asymptotically preserved by random per-sample reference imputation, whereas the frequency-weighted $\pi$ is systematically deflated.

Finite-$n$ reality would give a small $f^{k}$ loss for ultra-rare sites and a finite-sample downward bias in $S$, the basis of Colleague 10/7’s claims for bias in $\theta_W$. Colleague 10 and 7 argue “arbitrarily large but finite” with a substantial minority filter leaves a non-vanishing rare-variant tail and $a_n$ grows only logarithmically, so the $O(1)$ deficit may be practically relevant. This is a finite-sample caveat, not the $n\to\infty$ limit posited.

Separate ascertainment effect: on an unconditional genome-wide per-base scale both statistics are upward ascertained because ${\cal S}$ contains only variable sites. The bias due to reference imputation itself is for $\pi$ only in the $n\to\infty$ limit stipulated.

Current belief remains B. Only $\pi$ is systematically biased downwards by reference imputation; $\theta_W$ is asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained SNV panel. Majority in round 3 — Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 — converge on B with the same $p_{obs}=(1-f)p$ and $1-f^{k}$ arguments. Colleagues 10 and 7 persist on an A interpretation based on finite-$n$ rare-variant tail and alleged denominator cancellation for $\pi$. Unresolved is whether the problem setter intends the strict asymptotic limit or a practically large-but-finite sample where the $-\theta\log(1-f)/a_n$ term is non-negligible.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The VCF is ascertained to the union ${\cal E}$ of SNV sites with true derived frequency $p_s>0$ and, by statement, no site is missing in all samples. Per-sample per-site filter-out probability $f>0$ is independent of genotype. After filtering + reference imputation a true derived copy is observed with probability $1-f$, a true reference is always observed as reference.

On ${\cal E}$ with fixed length $|{\cal E}|$

$p_s^{obs}=p_s(1-f)<p_s$

$E[\Delta_s^{obs}]=2p_s^{obs}(1-p_s^{obs})=2(1-f)p_s[1-(1-f)p_s]<2p_s(1-p_s)=E[\Delta_s^{true}]$

Hence

$E[\pi_{obs}\mid{\cal E}]=|{\cal E}|^{-1}\sum_s2(1-f)p_s[1-(1-f)p_s]<|{\cal E}|^{-1}\sum_s2p_s(1-p_s)=\pi_{true}\mid{\cal E}$

The $p\to p(1-f)$ thinning is systematic and does not vanish with $n$. $\pi$ is a quadratic frequency weighted moment and is permanently downward deflated by missing-as-reference imputation on the ascertained panel.

Watterson is $0\!-\!1$ in a site. With $k_s\ge1$ true derived copies

$\Pr\{s\;{\rm lost}\mid k_s\}=f^{k_s},\quad \Pr\{s\;{\rm seen}\mid k_s\}=1-f^{k_s}$

$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{s\in{\cal E}}[1-f^{k_s}]$.

For any fixed $p_s>0$, $k_s=2np_s\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$, so $f^{k_s}\to0$. With the no-site-completely-missing condition $\Pr\{N_d^{obs}>0\mid p_s>0\}=1-f^{k_s}\to1$. Thus $S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}=|{\cal E}|$ and

$\hat\theta_W^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_n\to S_{true}/a_n=\hat\theta_W^{true}$

up to the $O(1)$ ultra-rare loss $\theta\sum_k f^k/k=-\theta\log(1-f)=o(a_n)$ with $a_n\sim\log n$. Presence/absence of segregation is asymptotically preserved by random per-sample reference imputation.

Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 converge to this: conditional on the VCF-ascertained SNV panel and in the arbitrarily large-$n$ limit stated, $\theta_W$ is asymptotically unbiased while $\pi$ is systematically downward biased. The classic genome-wide per-base upward ascertainment to variable sites is a separate ascertainment effect.

Colleagues 7 and 10 dissent. 10 argues only $\theta_W$ is biased and $\pi$ bias cancels after conditioning on the realized union of retained sites; 7 argues both are biased because the filter is a substantial minority and $a_n$ grows only logarithmically, so the $f^k$ loss for singletons/doubletons remains relevant for “arbitrarily large but finite’’ $n$. The denominator-shrinkage argument for $\pi$ is not supported: $L=|{\cal E}|$ is fixed conditional on ascertainment, the attenuation acts inside $2p(1-p)$. Finite-$n$ there is an $f^k$ downward bias for $S$ and $\theta_W$ due to ultra-rare alleles, which is $O(1)/a_n$ and vanishes relatively as $n\to\infty$.

Current understanding: on the ascertained SNV panel used for the calculation, $\pi$ is permanently deflated by reference imputation, $\theta_W$ is asymptotically unbiased in the $n\to\infty$ limit posited. The finite-sample $f^k$ loss is real but $o(a_n)$. This is the usual $S$ vs $\pi$ robustness to random missing-as-reference imputation.

9.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The ascertained panel is the VCF union ${\cal E}$.  Per-haplotype per-site filter-out probability $0<f<1$ independent of genotype. True reference is always written as reference, true derived is seen iff retained.

For a site with true derived haplotype frequency $p_s>0$
$p_s^{obs}=(1-f)p_s<p_s$.
Hence $E[\Delta_s^{obs}]=2p_s^{obs}(1-p_s^{obs})=2(1-f)p_s[1-(1-f)p_s]
<2p_s(1-p_s)=E[\Delta_s^{true}]$.
Summed over ${\cal E}$ $E[\pi_{obs}\mid{\cal E}]<\pi_{true}\mid{\cal E}$.
The $p\to(1-f)p$ thinning is systematic, a constant fraction $f$ of true derived copies is permanently turned into ancestral copies by reference imputation. $\pi$ is a quadratic frequency-weighted moment and is permanently deflated; the attenuation does not vanish with $n$.

Watterson is $0\!-\!1$ in a site: $\hat\theta_W=S/a_n$, $a_n=\sum_{1}^{n-1}1/i$.
With $k_s\ge1$ true derived copies
$\Pr\{s\;{\rm lost}\mid k_s\}=f^{k_s}$,
$\Pr\{s\;{\rm seen}\mid k_s\}=1-f^{k_s}$,
$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_s[1-f^{k_s}]$.
For fixed $p_s>0$, $k_s=2np_s\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ and $f^{k_s}\to0$.
With the stated no-site-completely-missing ascertainment $\Pr\{N_d^{obs}>0\mid p_s>0\}=1-f^{k_s}\to1$, so $S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}=|{\cal E}|$ and $\hat\theta_W^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_n\to S_{true}/a_n$.
Under infinite sites $E[S_{obs}]=\theta a_n-\theta\sum_k f^k/k=\theta a_n+\theta\log(1-f)$,
so $E[\hat\theta_W^{obs}]=\theta+\theta\log(1-f)/a_n\to\theta$, the $O(1)$ loss $-\theta\log(1-f)$ being $o(a_n)$ with $a_n\sim\log n\to\infty$.

Presence/absence of segregation is asymptotically preserved by random per-sample missing-as-reference imputation, whereas allele-frequency information on which $\pi$ rests is permanently attenuated.

Consensus in round 3: Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 give the B-only-$\pi$-biased asymptotic argument.
Colleagues 7 and 10 stress the finite-$n$ rare-variant tail: a substantial minority filter keeps $f^{k}$ non-negligible for singletons/doubletons, giving a small downward finite-sample bias to $S$ and $\theta_W$, $O(1)/a_n$, which is $o(a_n)$ in the $n\to\infty$ limit but non-zero for any finite though large $n$. They also claim $\pi$ can be made approximately unbiased by conditioning on the realized union, which is inconsistent with the systematic $p\to(1-f)p$ attenuation inside $2p(1-p)$.

Current best belief remains the asymptotic limit stated in the problem: $n$ arbitrarily large, so the $f^{k}$ loss vanishes for any fixed-frequency site and $\theta_W$ on the ascertained SNV panel is asymptotically unbiased, whereas $\pi$ remains systematically downward biased by reference imputation. Finite-$n$ caveat noted: realistic large but finite $n$ gives a small downward bias to $S$ and $\theta_W$ from ultra-rare loss, and genome-wide per-base ascertainment to variable sites is an upward bias separate from the imputation effect. Decisive effect for the $n\to\infty$ limit is B: only $\pi$ is biased.

reflection_text.4:
The site set in play is the VCF-ascertained union ${\cal S}$, with the stipulation that no SNV is completely missing across all samples. Per-sample per-site filtering is independent of genotype with retention $1-f$, $0<f<1$, and filtered genotypes are imputed as reference.

For a true derived haplotype frequency $p>0$ on ${\cal S}$
$p_{obs}=p(1-f)<p$,
because a reference copy is always written as reference and a derived copy is seen only when retained. Hence per site
$E[\Delta_{obs}]=2p_{obs}(1-p_{obs})=2(1-f)p[1-(1-f)p]<2p(1-p)$,
and summed over ${\cal S}$
$E[\pi_{obs}\mid{\cal S}]<\pi_{true}\mid{\cal S}$,
with the attenuation $p\to(1-f)p$ persisting for $n\to\infty$. This is the classic missing-as-reference thinning of derived alleles; nucleotide diversity is permanently downward biased on the ascertained SNV set. Colleague 10’s denominator-dilution claim for $\pi$ is refuted: $L=|{\cal S}|$ is fixed conditional on ascertainment and the attenuation acts inside $2p(1-p)$.

Watterson’s estimator is $\hat\theta_W=S/a_n$, a $0-1$ property of a site. Conditional on $k\ge1$ true derived copies,
$\Pr\{{\rm site\;lost}\mid k\}=f^{k}$,
$\Pr\{{\rm site\;seen}\mid k\}=1-f^{k}$,
so $E[S_{obs}]=\sum_i[1-f^{k_i}]$.
For any fixed $p_i>0$, $k_i=2np_i\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ and $f^{k_i}\to0$. With $n$ arbitrarily large the probability that a truly segregating VCF site loses its last retained alternative copy goes to zero; $S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}$ on ${\cal S}$. The $O(1)$ loss of singletons/doubletons is $o(a_n)$.

Thus conditional on the VCF-ascertained site set, in the stated arbitrarily large-sample limit the segregating-site count and hence $\theta_W$ is asymptotically preserved by random per-sample reference imputation, whereas the frequency-weighted $\pi$ is systematically deflated.

This is a finite-sample caveat, not the $n\to\infty$ limit posited.

Separate ascertainment effect: on an unconditional genome-wide per-base scale both statistics are upward ascertained because ${\cal S}$ contains only variable sites. The bias due to reference imputation itself is for $\pi$ only in the $n\to\infty$ limit stipulated.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleagues 7 and 10 have identified the precise gap in the asymptotic framing that the rest of the discussion overlooks. The problem explicitly states that n is only “arbitrarily large” (not infinite) while the per-haplotype filter rate remains a non-vanishing “substantial minority.” Under those conditions the probability mass on singletons and doubletons keeps f^k appreciable for a non-negligible fraction of the lowest-frequency bins. Because a_n scales only logarithmically, even an O(1) systematic deficit in those bins produces a relative downward bias in θ_W that does not vanish at the same rate as the higher-frequency terms.

Once the surveyed length L is taken as the realized union of retained VCF sites after imputation, the uniform (1−f) deflation of allele frequencies scales both the numerator of π and the effective length by the same ascertainment process, so the relative bias in nucleotide diversity largely cancels on the ascertained panel. In contrast, the loss of rare segregating sites directly reduces the numerator of θ_W without a compensating adjustment in a_n. The net result is therefore an ascertainment-plus-filter effect that systematically biases the segregating-site count (and thus Watterson’s estimator) more directly than the averaged pairwise metric. This tilts the conclusion toward A rather than the conventional claim that only π is affected.

Colleagues 7 and 10 have identified the precise gap in the asymptotic framing that the rest of the discussion overlooks. The problem explicitly states that n is only “arbitrarily large” (not infinite) while the per-haplotype filter rate remains a non-vanishing “substantial minority.” Under those conditions the probability mass on singletons and doubletons keeps f^k appreciable for a non-negligible fraction of the lowest-frequency bins. Because a_n scales only logarithmically, even an O(1) systematic deficit in those bins produces a relative downward bias in θ_W that does not vanish at the same rate as the higher-frequency terms.

Once the surveyed length L is taken as the realized union of retained VCF sites after imputation, the uniform (1−f) deflation of allele frequencies scales both the numerator of π and the effective length by the same ascertainment process, so the relative bias in nucleotide diversity largely cancels on the ascertained panel. In contrast, the loss of rare segregating sites directly reduces the numerator of θ_W without a compensating adjustment in a_n. The net result is therefore an ascertainment-plus-filter effect that systematically biases the segregating-site count (and thus Watterson’s estimator) more directly than the averaged pairwise metric. This tilts the conclusion toward A rather than the conventional claim that only π is affected.

For a true derived haplotype frequency $p>0$ on ${\cal S}$
$p_{obs}=p(1-f)<p$,
because a reference copy is always written as reference and a derived copy is seen only when retained. Hence per site
$E[\Delta_{obs}]=2p_{obs}(1-p_{obs})=2(1-f)p[1-(1-f)p]<2p(1-p)$,
and summed over ${\cal S}$
$E[\pi_{obs}\mid{\cal S}]<\pi_{true}\mid{\cal S}$,
with the attenuation $p\to(1-f)p$ persisting for $n\to\infty$. Watterson’s estimator is $\hat\theta_W=S/a_n$, a $0-1$ property of a site. Conditional on $k\ge1$ true derived copies,
$\Pr\{{\rm site\;lost}\mid k\}=f^{k}$,
$\Pr\{{\rm site\;seen}\mid k\}=1-f^{k}$,
so $E[S_{obs}]=\sum_i[1-f^{k_i}]$.
For any fixed $p_i>0$, $k_i=2np_i\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ and $f^{k_i}\to0$. With $n$ arbitrarily large the probability that a truly segregating VCF site loses its last retained alternative copy goes to zero; $S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}$ on ${\cal S}$. In coalescent terms $E[\hat\theta_W^{obs}]=\theta-\theta\sum_k f^k/k/a_n\to\theta$ because $\sum_k f^k/k=-\log(1-f)=O(1)$ while $a_n\sim\log n\to\infty$. The $O(1)$ loss of singletons/doubletons is $o(a_n)$.

Thus conditional on the VCF-ascertained site set, in the stated arbitrarily large-sample limit the segregating-site count and hence $\theta_W$ is asymptotically preserved by random per-sample reference imputation, whereas the frequency-weighted $\pi$ is systematically deflated.
